text.tspan: “Reuse last month's update as the style

svg.text: ONE LINE VS A REAL BRIEF

text.tspan: No audience, no facts, no format — the model has to guess all three.
“Draft a 300-word status update for the steering committee. The vendor
slipped two weeks; mitigation is agreed. Three sections, neutral tone,
Same effort to type. A usable first draft instead of filler.
Paste the real material — source grounding is your biggest accuracy
“Act as a sceptical CFO” surfaces objections a neutral voice never
Name the sections, length and order you want.
One sample beats five adjectives every time.
“Keep the structure, rewrite section two with the delay detail.”
Starting over throws away the half that already worked.
No paste, no context — the model cannot invent your facts.
Too many jobs at once. Split it into clear, separate tasks.
“Make it punchy and professional” — show an example instead.
First draft weak? Refine once before blaming the tool.
New task means a new chat. Old context quietly misleads.
A perfect prompt does not replace verification, fairness checks, approved
tools or minimising the data you paste.

svg.text: Before you send: scan for Task · Context · Format · Constraints · Examples — every missing block is a guess the AI has to make.
